gloss: Before dismissing a distinction as too complicated, state what decision it would change
mechanism: A distinction proposed for dismissal as too complicated is first tested: state which {{decision}} or prediction would change if it were kept. A distinction that changes nothing may be dropped; one that changes something is kept, whatever it costs to state.
invariants: A dismissed distinction carries a statement of what it would have changed.
A distinction that would change a decision or prediction is not dismissed for its length.
failure_modes: Slogan win: the shorter account is preferred because it is shorter.
Complexity hoard: every distinction is kept whether or not it changes anything.
